title: Count Reachable Rooms (Graph DFS)
real_world_story: Before sending a robot into a wing, the controller must know how many rooms the robot can ever enter from its starting room, so cleaning or inspection jobs are never assigned to sealed-off areas.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Rooms and the corridors joining them
real_world_connection.query_represents: The room the robot starts in
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Walking one corridor as far as possible and backtracking to try the next one

problem_statement: Given N rooms numbered 0 to N-1 and E corridors, plus a starting room S, count every room the robot can reach from S using any number of corridor moves. A room counts itself as reachable.
task: Return the number of rooms reachable from S, including S itself.
input_format: The first line contains three integers N, M and D with D = 0 for undirected corridors and D = 1 for one-way doorways. The next M lines each contain two integers u v. The final line contains the start room S.
output_format: Print the number of rooms reachable from S, including S itself.

examples.explanation: From room 0 the robot can walk along the whole chain 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, so all 5 rooms are reachable.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: Following one corridor as far as it goes and backtracking to unvisited branches visits every room of the connected region exactly once, which is depth-first search.

complexity.time: O(N + M) because every room and corridor is processed once
complexity.space: O(N + M) for the adjacency list and the visited marks

hint: Keep a visited mark per room so sealed loops cannot trap the search.
Push newly found rooms and always finish one branch before trying the next.
Each room lands in the region exactly once, so the count equals the number of marked rooms.
real_world_takeaway: Depth-first mapping visits every reachable room exactly once, so the robot knows its whole territory in a single walk.
